title: fix(runtime)!: an artifact holding two enabled jobs of one name schedules neither, refused at bind naming both, instead of the job service silently keeping the later
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-bill"} -->
_Requested by **Bill** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wg?thread=cmsg_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wg3kiV8PawtFeYMMXHqAu5kD)_

domain:server#2 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CaP1iy4RSEQbW6177G

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：一个制品里如果有两个（或更多）启用中的同名 job，启动或安装时两个都不排程，在 `error` 级别记一条带 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`（409）的拒绝，点名每个声明方和每个 job 的运行方式；以前排过的同名 job 一并停掉。其他名字的 job 照常运行。
- 为什么改：job 服务按名字存 job，第二次排程会替换第一次。改前两个同名 job 只剩后排的那个在跑，另一个永远不跑，也没有任何日志，运维看不到信号（Cron 与 Interval 两个适配器、两种残余归属都实测如此）。
- 风险与回滚：收窄（BREAKING，第一方计数 0）：两个包体同名 job、包体与无 manifest 输入同名 job、或手写 JSON 制品里同名列两次，改前能启动（一个被静默丢掉），改后两个都不排程。禁用的那个不算冲突。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts` 的 `jobNameCollisions`（按名字数启用的 job，组装拒绝信息）和 `scheduleAppArtifactJobs` 里它被调用、写进 `refused` 的两处。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/app-artifact-handlers.job-pull.test.ts`，预期 60 个用例全绿；`[#32411]` 下 12 个是本卡新增。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

Fixes #32411

Clause-②: no (narrowing)

The narrowing: `scheduleAppArtifactJobs` answers an artifact whose enabled jobs share a name FROM both bound under one job-service key, the later replacing the earlier (`CronJobAdapter.schedule`, `IntervalJobAdapter.store`), the earlier never running and nothing logged TO neither scheduled, each named in the result's new `refused` list, and one `error` line per name carrying a `PackageScopedNameRefusedError` (`RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, 409, `ambiguous-in-environment`) naming every holder and each job's run form. A job of that name an earlier install scheduled FROM kept running TO cancelled (named in `cancelled`). First-party census: 0 (the one first-party job, `showcase_health_sweep`, has its own name; `examples/app-multi-package` declares no job). A pair whose other enabled twin would not have been scheduled on its own (a `pull` whose mapping is missing or sourceless, a `handler` the bundle does not carry, no `organization` under `isolated`, a schedule the adapter throws on) FROM exactly one job scheduled and running, the other named at `warn` or `error`, TO neither scheduled, both in `refused` (row G). Every result gains the additive `refused: []` member (the `withheld` returns too) and the closing summary line `refused: 0`; nothing else moves for an artifact with no shared job name. The Claim's bare declaration is the same one; the seat ruled the narrowing arm on step 0.

Metadata-protocol: none — no key, value or schema changes; `defineStack` already refuses two jobs of one name inside one stack, and what moves is the runtime's answer to a composition or a JSON artifact that carries the pair.
Skills-docs: `content/docs/automation/jobs.mdx` — one paragraph added under the job's `name` (an artifact cannot hold two enabled jobs of one name; none is scheduled, refused at `error` with 409) and the "Which mapping a name reads" sentence on two bodies' job name corrected (both enabled ⇒ neither scheduled; one disabled ⇒ the other's run refused 409, as before). No sentence under `skills/` teaches job names across packages (grep of `skills/` for job name, duplicate, same name, `409` near jobs: no hit).

## Why

A job service keys a job by its name and replaces the job it already holds under that name, which is what lets a reinstall replace its own job. The binder schedules every job of one artifact under the artifact's id, so two jobs of one name collapsed into one: the earlier never ran and nothing said so (card #32411, measured on both real adapters and both residual owner arrangements, table below). Never keep one job silently: nothing picks one of them, so the name is refused, the way ADR-0150 D3 refuses an ambiguous name, and the refusal is said where an operator reads.

## What changes

- **`jobNameCollisions(bundle, appId, jobs)`** (new, `packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts`): counts the artifact's ENABLED jobs by name (the list `scheduleAppArtifactJobs` binds, `collectBundleJobs`); every name two or more share gets a `PackageScopedRefusal` (`type: 'job'`, `reason: 'ambiguous-in-environment'`, `callerPackageId: null`). Its holders are every body declaring the name and, when the artifact holds more jobs of the name than its bodies declare, the artifact's top level outside every body (the residual: by count, never by content, the rule `jobDeclaringPackages` uses for #32355); an artifact without `packages[]` is its app's alone. Its `candidates` are every declaring body as a `package`, then, where the top level carries the name too, the residual as `{ kind: 'residual', ownerId }` (the artifact's id; the holder kind #32412 added to core, as `jobNameRefusal` names it); an artifact without `packages[]` names the app itself. The message names each holder and each job's run form (`pulls mapping "X"`, `runs a sandboxed body`, `runs handler "X"`).
- **`scheduleAppArtifactJobs`**: after the scheduled-work and job-service gates, the refusals are computed once and each is logged at `error` with a `PackageScopedNameRefusedError` (code `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, status 409; an existing ledgered code, no spec change). In the per-job loop, right after the `enabled: false` skip, a job whose name is refused is pushed to the new `refused` list and not scheduled. `retireAppJobs` then cancels a job of that name the app scheduled before, as for any job the call no longer schedules. The closing summary line carries `refused`.
- **`AppArtifactJobScheduling.refused: string[]`** (new member of an exported runtime interface; additive, one entry per job, as the other lists).
- **`bodyJobDeclarations`**: the package-body walk `jobDeclaringPackages` already did, extracted so both read one walk; `jobDeclaringPackages` answers exactly as before (its #32071 / #32355 assertions are unchanged and green).
- A disabled job is scheduled by nothing, so it collides with nothing and is not counted: its enabled twin is scheduled as before, and a pull's run keeps the run-time attribution refusal (#32355's fail-closed pin, unchanged).
- The adapters are untouched: replace-by-name is their documented contract, and a reinstall relies on it.

## FROM → TO (every moved answer)

Measured on `main` `d8a2f0d2` (FROM, the step-0 probe, both real adapters, identical on each) and this head (TO).

| # | Artifact | FROM (CronJobAdapter and IntervalJobAdapter) | TO |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | body `alpha` declares pull job `sync`; a manifest-less input declares `sync` too; residual runs as `beta` | both bound, one key; the survivor's run refused 409 (#32355), the other job gone, no log line | neither scheduled; `refused: ['sync','sync']`; one 409 refusal at error naming `alpha`, the top level, `alpha_map`, `host_map`; candidates `[package alpha, residual(beta)]` |
| B | same pair; residual runs as `alpha`, the declaring body | both bound, one key; `alpha_map` runs as `alpha`, `host_map` never runs, no warn or error | neither scheduled; same refusal; candidates `[package alpha, residual(alpha)]` |
| C | two package bodies each declare body-form job `tick` | both bound, one key; one silently dropped | neither scheduled; refusal candidates `[gamma, delta]` |
| D | single-package JSON artifact lists `twice` twice (no build judged it) | both bound, one key; one silently dropped | neither scheduled; candidates `[the app]`; a job of its own name in the same artifact still runs |
| E | reinstall of D after a version that declared `twice` once | — | the earlier `twice` cancelled (`cancelled: ['twice']`), nothing left on the job service |
| F | #32071 pin: two bodies each declare pull job `sync` | both bound, each run refused 409 | neither scheduled, one 409 refusal at bind naming both packages |
| G | two enabled jobs `paired`, one of which cannot be scheduled on its own (here a pull naming a mapping the artifact lacks) | no shared key: the binding one scheduled and runs, the other `notScheduled` at warn | neither scheduled, both in `refused`; one 409 refusal |

`composeStacks(…, { manifest: 'preserve' })` accepted A and C (measured), and D reaches the binder through no build at all, so the build side is not the only honest place; the refusal lives at the one binder both doors schedule through (`AppPlugin` and `MarketplaceInstallLocal`).

## Tests

`packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.job-pull.test.ts`, new `describe('[#32411] two enabled jobs of one name in one artifact are refused at bind, naming both')`, on the real `CronJobAdapter` and `IntervalJobAdapter`:

- for each adapter × both residual owner arrangements: neither job scheduled, `refused` names both, nothing on the job service, no pull, exactly one `{ code: 'RESOURCE_CONFLICT', status: 409 }` refusal naming the body package, both mappings and the top level, its candidates `[package alpha, residual(artifact id)]`;
- CONTROL, each adapter × arrangement: one job of each name binds and runs `success` as today, no refusal;
- two bodies' body-form jobs: refused, candidates both packages;
- a single-package JSON artifact listing a name twice: refused, the job of another name runs;
- a twin that would not have bound still refuses the name: the twin that binds is not scheduled either (row G; ablation: red, then restored);
- a refused name cancels the job an earlier install scheduled.

The fixtures the #32355 suite used (`alpha`, `host`, `beta`, `jsonLoaded`, `scheduleAndRun`) moved to module scope, and `scheduleAndRun` takes the adapter. Three existing pins move with the fix (their `jobDeclaringPackages` assertions unchanged): #32071 "two bodies each declaring job `sync`" (FROM each run refused TO refused at bind), #32355 "JSON-loaded, on a real job service" (FROM `out.pulls ['sync','sync']` and a failed run TO `refused` and nothing scheduled), #32355 "control: the residual's owner IS the one declaring body" (FROM the body's copy running TO refused at bind; the one-holder attribution still asserted), and #32355 "controls: a residual job with a name of its own…" drops the `sync` run row. #32412's real-`CronJobAdapter` pin (merged from main) now reads both twins enabled as refused at bind (`refused` both, nothing scheduled, the bind refusal's candidates `[package alpha, residual(top)]`) and keeps its run-record half with the body's twin disabled (the run refused, the same candidates). The fixtures both PRs hoisted to module scope are one block. `app-artifact-handlers.jobs.test.ts` "a disabled job is skipped on every form" gains `refused: []` in its whole-result equality.

<details><summary>Red first, green, ablation</summary>

- Red on main + pins (0252ae53): `Tests 11 failed | 43 passed (54)`, exactly the 11 new `[#32411]` cases.
- Green (9d82ba29): `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/app-artifact-handlers.job-pull.test.ts src/app-artifact-handlers.jobs.test.ts src/app-artifact-handlers.job-pull-run.test.ts` → `Test Files 3 passed (3)`, `Tests 101 passed (101)`.
- Ablation (once, `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, through the verify lock): anchor `if (shared.length === 0) return refusals;` → `if (shared.length >= 0) return refusals; // ABLATION-32411` (x1 → x0, blob f75b12fb3e20 → b527ef0f59ba), `Tests 11 failed | 43 passed (54)`: the 7 refusal pins plus the 4 moved existing pins red, every CONTROL green; restored, blob == HEAD f75b12fb3e20, `git diff HEAD` empty. The source is read from `src/` (relative import), so no build leg.

- Round 2 (582fcbfac): pin "a twin that would not have bound still refuses the name" (row G); job-pull `Tests 55 passed (55)`; ablation with the same anchor, `-t 'would not have bound'`: `1 failed`, restored, blob == HEAD.
- Round 3 (30c29d52, after #32567): job-pull + jobs + job-pull-run `Tests 107 passed (107)`. Ablation once, `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: delete `candidates.push({ kind: 'residual', ownerId: appId });` (x1 → x0, blob 1f9f63918300 → 96bd0e773b7a) → `Tests 5 failed | 55 passed (60)`: the four adapter × arrangement refusal pins and #32412's real-adapter pin; restored, blob == HEAD 1f9f63918300, `git diff HEAD` empty.

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- Supersedes, in the same release (declared in the changeset): the pending `32071-pull-reads-mapping-by-job-package` item 4 and the `32355-residual-job-twin-refused` sentence on each run being refused, for the both-enabled case; both stay true with one twin disabled.

- `DbJobAdapter.schedule` delegates to `CronJobAdapter` / `IntervalJobAdapter` (`register`), so it replaces by name the same way; not measured separately.
- The install-local door's up-front refusal (`collectJobsWithoutBody`, a 422 on install) does not judge duplicate names; such a package installs (200) and its jobs of the shared name are refused at bind with the error line. Filed by the seat as #32572; not fixed here.
